app.name: Crop Yield AI
app.tagline: Know your harvest before you sow

common.offline: You appear to be offline. Saved pages still work.

home.title: Know your harvest before you sow.
home.subtitle: Enter your field's soil, weather and water. Get a yield estimate with an honest range, the reasons behind it, and what to change to earn more.
home.f1_d: Every estimate comes with an 80% interval, so you can plan for the good and the bad season.
home.f2_d: SHAP shows which factors added or cost you tonnes per hectare: water, pH, temperature, soil.
home.f3_d: Irrigation, lime, urea, super phosphate and potash quantities, with the yield gain the model expects from each.
home.f4_d: Same field, ten crops: yield, cost and profit side by side.
home.s1: Describe the field or tap “use my location” to fetch live weather.
home.s2: The model predicts yield and its uncertainty.
home.s3: Read the drivers and recommendations, simulate changes, download the PDF.
home.langs: Available in English, हिन्दी and ಕನ್ನಡ. Speak your values with the microphone. Installs on your phone like an app.
home.disclaimer: Estimates are decision support, not guarantees. Confirm fertiliser and lime doses with a soil test.

insights.title: Model insights
insights.subtitle: How the model was built, how well it performs, and what it relies on.
insights.cov_text: Nominal 80% interval covered {{c}}% of unseen fields (raw quantile model: {{r}}%). Average width {{w}} t/ha.
insights.resid_text: Residual mean {{m}} t/ha, std {{s}} t/ha, skew {{k}}. A mean near zero means no systematic bias; negative skew means a few large over-predictions.

dash.sub: Here is where your fields stand.

data.synthetic_text: This model was trained on SIMULATED farms, not real records. Use it to explore how the system works, not as evidence about real yields.
data.real_text: Trained on government district yield statistics (observed). Weather and soil are regional estimates for the district, not measurements at your field, so the result is a district-level average.
data.observed_d: District yield records from government statistics (area and production).
data.estimate_d: Weather and soil at the district centre from gridded datasets, not measured at your field.
data.simulated_d: Generated by an agronomic simulator for prototyping and tests.
data.district_help: Soil and location are looked up from the district. These are regional estimates.
data.soil_from_district: Soil properties come from the selected district (regional estimate), not from a test of your field.
data.split: Chronological evaluation: trained on {{train}}, validated on {{val}}, tested on {{test}}.
data.per_region: Accuracy by state (most recent test years)

health.title: Crop health from space
health.subtitle: See how green your field looks in satellite images (Sentinel-2 NDVI) and spot areas that may need a closer look.
health.refreshing: Asking the satellite service… this can take 10 to 30 seconds.
health.unconfigured_title: Satellite monitoring is not set up on this server
health.unconfigured_text: The administrator needs to add the Google Earth Engine settings (GEE_PROJECT and credentials). You can still save fields now.
health.no_fields_text: Add your farmland to see its satellite crop-health map.
health.delete_confirm: Delete this field and its saved observations?
health.name: Field name
health.method: How do you want to mark the field?
health.pick_hint: Tap the map to place the centre of your field.
health.draw_hint: Tap the map to add the corners of your field in order. You need at least 3.
health.coords_hint: Latitude then longitude, in degrees. Check that the pin lands on your field.
health.bad_coords: Enter valid coordinates (latitude -56 to 84, longitude -180 to 180).
health.clear_sky: {{p}}% of the field was clear of clouds
health.legend_note: Approximate boundaries: below {{low}} red, {{low}} to {{high}} yellow, {{high}} and above green. They vary by crop and growth stage.
health.cat_low_text: The vegetation looks sparse or not very green. This can mean bare soil, a young or newly sown crop, a harvested or fallow field, or crop stress.
health.cat_moderate_text: The vegetation is moderately green. This is common at early or late growth stages or with a partial canopy, and it can also reflect stress.
health.cat_high_text: The vegetation looks dense and green across most of the field.
health.change_up: Greenness rose by {{d}} over {{n}} days, consistent with canopy growth.
health.change_down: Greenness fell by {{d}} over {{n}} days. This can come from ripening, harvest or stress. Inspect the field before concluding anything.
health.change_flat: Greenness is broadly unchanged ({{d}}) since the previous observation.
health.caveats_title: What NDVI can and cannot tell you
health.caveat_1: NDVI shows how green the vegetation looks from space. It is not a diagnosis of crop health.
health.caveat_2: It cannot identify a specific disease, pest, or nutrient or water problem.
health.caveat_3: Low values can also mean bare soil, a newly sown or harvested field, a different growth stage, or mixed pixels at the field edge.
health.caveat_4: Satellite pixels are 10 m wide, so small or narrow fields and edges are less reliable.
health.caveat_5: Compare with the same crop at the same growth stage, and check the field on the ground before acting.
health.disclaimer: Vegetation greenness indicator, not a diagnosis.
health.history_one: Only one clear observation so far. A trend needs at least two.
health.history_note: Dashed lines mark the approximate colour boundaries.
health.no_data_text: No cloud-free Sentinel-2 image covering enough of this field was found in the last {{n}} days. This is common in the monsoon. Try a longer period or check again in a few days. Nothing has been estimated.
health.layer_error: The map layer could not be loaded, but the NDVI value above is still valid.
health.tiles_error: Map tiles failed to load. Press Refresh from satellite to get a new map link.
health.source: Sentinel-2 (ESA Copernicus), 10 m. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data. Revisits about every 5 days when not cloudy.
health.select_field: Select a field to see its crop-health map.
